title: ActRaiser
subtitle: Quintet · Super Nintendo Entertainment System

body: ActRaiser is Quintet's Super Nintendo game combining side-scrolling action with the development of human settlements. As the Master, the player descends into dangerous regions through an animated warrior statue, then guides the people who begin living there. An angel protects the growing community from above. The two perspectives give victory a consequence that can be watched: after the monsters are defeated, roads and houses appear where the action has made settlement possible. The next journey begins with seeing what those people still need.

During the overhead sections, the player directs construction and uses miracles such as rain, sunlight and lightning to make the land habitable. The angel shoots at monsters threatening the population, while expanding settlements eventually seal the lairs producing them. More inhabitants increase the Master's strength, linking the quiet work of planning to survival in the action stages. The player has to understand the region before choosing the right intervention. A field, an obstructed route and a dangerous nest each call for a different kind of help.

Each region includes action sequences in which the warrior crosses platforms, attacks monsters and confronts a boss. Those encounters bracket the slower development of the community, giving the campaign a rhythm between direct struggle and watching its results. Yuzo Koshiro's score uses the Super Nintendo's sound capabilities for an orchestral character that helped distinguish this early release. Published by Enix in Japan in 1990, ActRaiser made its unusual combination coherent by giving both halves the same purpose: recover a place and make life there possible.
story_headings: First fight, then help a world grow
A new console finds a musical voice
